transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-29 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52m
Attendees: Jordan Park (Redwood AE), Mira Chen (Redwood SE), Asha Patel (CTO, Onyx), Luis Ortega (Senior DevOps), Riley Kim (Security Engineer), Samir Rao (ML Engineer)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Discussed POC topology: aim to keep inference in eu-west-1, evaluate privatelink vs vpc peering, measure p95 latency and cost per 1k tokens, security requirements include SOC2, KMS encryption, audit logs and SSO.

---- Transcript ----
[00:00] Jordan Park: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll kick off, quick intros — mine's Jordan, i'm the AE, Mira is our SE, we're here to scope the pilot for network and residency stuff.
[00:18] Asha Patel: hi, thanks. quick context — Onyx handles patient-derived assay metadata, so residency is non-negotiable, we'll need eu-west-1 for now. We're trying to avoid adding a full on-prem stack.
[00:35] Mira Chen: got it. for the pilot, do you anticipate a lot of long context windows or mostly short prompts? that'll change sizing and kernel choices.
[00:47] Samir Rao: mostly short, 100-200 tokens typical, occasionally 1k token analysis but rare. QPS target is around 60-100 qps for the initial service.
[01:05] Luis Ortega: security note, our infra team prefers VPC peering but some compliance folks push for privatelink because it avoids route table exposure. we want to hear tradeoffs.
[01:20] Mira Chen: OK. summary of tradeoffs — VPC peering gives lower latency and direct network path, but requires peering across accounts and managing route tables; PrivateLink uses an endpoint service and is easier for isolation and avoids broad peering but can add a hop and sometimes extra NAT/egress paths which impact egress constraints.
[01:45] Riley Kim: can you expand on the egress concerns? our legal team wants zero outbound to non-eu IPs.
[01:54] Jordan Park: yep, totally — we can lock inference to eu-west-1 for the pilot and restrict egress. our private deployment supports region-locking and can use customer-managed VPC endpoints; if you use privatelink, we can ensure service endpoints are in the eu-west region and provide a limited set of egress FQDNs.
[02:15] Asha Patel: what's realistic for latency p95? we need to set an SLO.
[02:22] Mira Chen: from past pilots — with a small model variant and good instance types in eu-west-1, p95 token latency for short prompts sits around 120-220ms when warmed and with KV cache enabled. for very bursty workloads you may see spikes; that's why we recommend continuous batching and a steady warmup.
[02:45] Samir Rao: can you quantify batching? we worry batchization will increase tail latency.
[02:52] Mira Chen: sure — we use workload-aware batching; for inference with 100-200 token prompts, a batch size of 8-16 often balances throughput and tail latency. we can tune threshold-based batching so low-latency requests pass through; also prefix caching will reduce tokens computed for repeated contexts.
[03:14] Luis Ortega: what about KV cache — we use long running sessions for some flows, how's cache state handled across nodes and peering?
[03:24] Mira Chen: KV cache is per-inference-runtime but replicated across shards; if your requests hit different nodes, we either pin sessions or use sticky routing. in Private deployments we can expose session affinity. note: sometimes transcriber shows kv cash in logs, ignore that.
[03:45] Jordan Park: quick check on success criteria — what are the must-haves? Asha?
[03:52] Asha Patel: must-haves: all inference stays in eu-west-1, no egress to non-eu, audit logs stored for 12 months, SSO/SAML integration with our IdP, and 99% uptime during business hours.
[04:07] Riley Kim: and we need KMS with customer-managed keys, plus evidence of rotation and key lifecycle.
[04:14] Jordan Park: yep, all doable — we'll include KMS notes in security pack.
[04:19] Samir Rao: on benchmarks, we want to replicate our real prompt mix. can Redwood run a bench that matches our QPS and prompt set?
[04:28] Mira Chen: yes — we'll ask you for a sample prompt set (anonymized) and expected QPS / concurrency. we'll run a two-phase bench: control (peering) and privatelink if needed, measure p95 latency, p99, and tokens/sec.
[04:45] Luis Ortega: timeline? we need a pilot within ~3 weeks to present to compliance.
[04:50] Jordan Park: propose: week 1 — exchange network and security artifacts; week 2 — run bench and validate configs; week 3 — review results and handoff. that would put review meeting around 2026-05-20. does that align?
[05:11] Asha Patel: yes, that's reasonable if you can deliver security docs quickly.
[05:17] Mira Chen: i'll prep the sizing spreadsheet — rough calc based on your QPS 80 and 200 token avg suggests starting with 4 x A100-sized instances (or equivalent local GPU profile) for sustained throughput, with burst headroom. we'll include a quantized option to lower cost if accuracy acceptable.
[05:38] Samir Rao: can you include expected cost delta between hosted and dedicated? we want a rough run-rate.
[05:44] Jordan Park: yes, we'll include a run-rate and an ops note: dedicated/reserved reduces unit cost but adds commit; hosted pilot keeps things simple.
[05:54] Riley Kim: regarding privatelink egress — if the service uses NAT, can you guarantee egress IPs stay in eu-west-1?
[06:02] Mira Chen: we'll provide a bounded list of IPs/FQDNs and can route via region-local NAT gateways; for privatelink there's an extra step to register endpoint ENIs in your VPC, but traffic stays in-region. we'll document specific egress endpoints in the security pack.
[06:21] Luis Ortega: about peering — we'd have to open up route tables to Redwood account, and our infra folks want to avoid broad CIDR overlap. do you support prefix-lists to limit routes?
[06:33] Mira Chen: yes we can accept prefix lists and we recommend non-overlapping CIDRs; if overlap exists, PrivateLink avoids that.
[06:40] Jordan Park: let's capture actions — Jordan will send the security pack, Mira will size, Onyx will share CIDRs and sample prompts.
[06:48] Asha Patel: quick Q — do you support audit log exports into our S3?
[06:52] Jordan Park: yes, we can stream audit logs to customer S3 or push via SIEM connectors; we'll include details.
[07:01] Samir Rao: any expected blockers?
[07:05] Mira Chen: only potential blocker is if compliance demands full air-gapped on-prem; otherwise either privatelink or peering will work. if air-gap needed we'd shift to our Private on-prem package which has a longer timeline.
[07:21] Luis Ortega: can you run a short network test before the benchmark window? like simple pings/traceroute to measure RTT?
[07:28] Mira Chen: yes — we'll coordinate a 1-hour network smoke test (TCP handshake and TLS) during the week of 2026-05-11. Jordan will PM to schedule.
[07:38] Riley Kim: please include SAML metadata flow diagram for SSO and the minimal entitlements required.
[07:44] Jordan Park: will do.
[07:47] Mira Chen: ok last bit — what are the acceptance criteria numerically?
[07:52] Asha Patel: acceptance: p95 latency under 300ms for our short prompts, p99 under 600ms, sustained 60-80 qps with no missing KV state, 99% availability during business hours, audit and KMS controls verified.
[08:10] Jordan Park: noted. we'll run benches against those targets and surface regressions.
[08:15] Asha Patel: perfect. thanks everyone.
[08:18] Jordan Park: thanks — we'll recap with actions in an email and share docs.

End transcript.
